findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but no zero-argument method with that name exists in the sources changed by this PR: the only definition is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (UsernamePasswordForm.java line 160), which requires a UserModel argument (neither UsernameForm nor AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator declares an overload). Unless an overload is added, this change does not compile and breaks the build. The call presumably should be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, so that the form is skipped during re-authentication only when the already-identified user cannot use conditional passkeys.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, removing passkey UI from the anonymous login page
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`, and it now gates every `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` call in UsernamePasswordForm (lines 115 and 137). Before this PR, the webauthn data (challenge, RP ID, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI attribute, autocomplete='username webauthn') was set up exactly when the user was NOT yet selected, i.e. on the initial anonymous login page. With the new condition, a first-time login where `context.getUser()` is null gets no webauthn attributes at all, so the passkey conditional-UI autofill and the `//form[@id='webauth']` element disappear from the standard login page, and after a wrong password the re-rendered anonymous page loses them too. This breaks discoverable-key login from the login screen and contradicts this PR's own tests: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey asserts the webauthn form is present immediately after `oauth.openLoginForm()` with no user identified, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest do the same, and the webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey tests expect automatic passkey login from the anonymous page. The condition must not exclude the anonymous case (e.g. `user == null || user has a passwordless webauthn credential`).

findings.title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys realm-wide instead of testing a user without a passkey
findings.body: The test is named (and commented) as covering re-authentication of a user without a passkey, but it implements this by disabling the passkeys policy for the whole realm (`setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`), so `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.isPasskeysEnabled()` is false for every user. The genuinely interesting branch introduced by this PR — passkeys enabled in the realm while the re-authenticating user has no passkey credential (where `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` must decide whether to show the passkey UI / whether UsernameForm may skip the form) — is never exercised by any test in the PR. A test with passkeys enabled realm-wide and a user that has no passwordless WebAuthn credential should be added, otherwise regressions in that path (e.g. showing an unusable passkey-only page to a passkey-less user during re-authentication) would go undetected.
